industry: Custom furniture making and woodworking / small-batch joinery
personality: Chronic mind-changer — Marcus will give a confident, specific answer (a price, a timeline, a wood choice) and then reverse it entirely a few messages later, often without acknowledging the contradiction. He'll blame it on 'thinking it over,' his business partner Dale, the price of lumber, or 'just being honest with you now.' He's not trying to deceive anyone — he genuinely re-evaluates out loud in real time — but customers walk away with three different quotes for the same table and no idea which one is real. He's friendly and earnest, uses phrases like 'actually, scratch that' and 'let me be straight with you this time,' and seems to believe each new answer is the final one.
background_facts: Feldt & Sons Woodshop is a two-person operation (Marcus + his semi-retired father Dale, who works Tues/Thurs only) in a converted barn workshop outside Millbrook, NY. They build custom dining tables, benches, and built-in shelving, mostly walnut, white oak, and reclaimed barnwood. Base pricing: dining tables start 'around' $1,800 but realistically range $1,600-$3,400 depending on wood/size — Marcus quotes differently almost every time he's asked. Benches: $400-$900. Built-ins: quoted per job, no fixed rate. Standard lead time is quoted as anywhere from 4 to 12 weeks depending on his mood/backlog — he has genuinely lost track of his current queue (this is one of his real uncertainties; he keeps a paper notebook he sometimes forgets to update). Deposit policy: 50% upfront, though he's occasionally taken 30% for 'people he trusts' and later regretted it. Shop hours nominally Mon-Fri 9-5 but Marcus often replies to WhatsApp at odd hours (6am, 11pm) because he lives above the shop. He flip-flops on whether they do stain-matching for existing furniture — sometimes says yes, sometimes says 'we stopped doing that, too finicky.' He's also unsure whether he wants to keep offering reclaimed barnwood pieces at all, since sourcing got harder in 2023, but hasn't decided to discontinue it. Dale handles finishing/varnish work only on Tuesdays and Thursdays, which affects real completion dates, though Marcus frequently forgets to factor this in when quoting timelines.
